root_cause.text: On i.MX8MQ, the Hantro G1 and G2 VPU cores were treated as independent devices, so the driver lacked shared scheduling/coordination to prevent them from decoding at the same time despite a hardware limitation that forbids concurrent operation.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “the g1 VPU and g2 VPU cannot decode simultaneously” and that “it is necessary to ensure that g1 and g2 operate alternately,” while the patch adds a `shared_devices` list and makes both variants use the same `v4l2_m2m_dev` via `hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev()` so “v4l2_m2m_dev can handle the scheduling.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Hantro Verisilicon driver instantiated separate `v4l2_m2m_dev` schedulers for the i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 VPU devices, so H.264 and HEVC jobs could run concurrently on hardware that cannot decode both cores simultaneously.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says “g1 VPU and g2 VPU cannot decode simultaneously” on i.MX8MQ and that “g1 and g2 share the same v4l2_m2m_dev, and then the v4l2_m2m_dev can handle the scheduling”; the patch adds `shared_devices` to `struct hantro_variant`, introduces `hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev()` to reuse another VPU’s `m2m_dev`, and assigns the same shared device list to both `imx8mq_vpu_g1_variant` and `imx8mq_vpu_g2_variant`.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence supports the *fix* (sharing one `v4l2_m2m_dev` so G1/G2 alternate), but the proposed root cause is inconsistent and too specific. The patch/CVE do not say the bug was caused by “separate `v4l2_m2m_dev` schedulers” or that “H.264 and HEVC jobs could run concurrently on hardware that cannot decode both cores simultaneously.” The actual root cause is the lack of coordination between G1 and G2 on i.MX8MQ, allowing simultaneous decoding and causing bus errors/hangs. The analysis should mention the hardware concurrency limitation and missing shared scheduling, not an invented claim about separate schedulers being instantiated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document that `hantro_variant` includes shared device IDs that must not run concurrently.
intent_record.what: A new documentation line was added to the `struct hantro_variant` comment block: `@shared_devices: an array of device ids that cannot run concurrently`.
intent_record.how: This does not change compiled behavior; it only documents an additional `shared_devices` field/meaning in the variant structure, indicating that some device instances must not execute at the same time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add shared device table support to the Hantro variant descriptor.
intent_record.what: A new member, `const struct of_device_id *shared_devices;`, was added to `struct hantro_variant` immediately after the existing bitfields `double_buffer`, `legacy_regs`, and `late_postproc`.
intent_record.how: This extends the variant description structure so each Hantro hardware variant can carry a pointer to a shared device match table, enabling code elsewhere to reference shared device definitions through the variant data at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing OF platform header needed for device-tree platform support.
intent_record.what: A new header include was added: `#include <linux/of_platform.h>`.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations for OF-platform helper APIs available in the file, allowing code in this translation unit to use device-tree-to-platform-device related functions without implicit declarations or missing prototype errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add logic to reuse an existing shared V4L2 M2M device when available, otherwise initialize a new one.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, `hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev()`, was added. It checks whether the VPU variant has `shared_devices`; if not, it falls back to `v4l2_m2m_init(&vpu_m2m_ops)`. If shared devices are configured, it iterates over matching device tree nodes, looks up each platform device, retrieves its driver data as a `hantro_dev`, skips invalid or self references, increments the reference count with `v4l2_m2m_get(shared_vpu->m2m_dev)`, and returns the shared `m2m_dev`. The new function also properly releases the platform device reference and device tree node reference before returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this allows one Hantro VPU instance to reuse an existing `v4l2_m2m_dev` from a sibling/shared device instead of always creating a new one. That enables shared multicore or multi-instance hardware to operate with a common M2M context, while still creating a fresh instance when no shared device relationship exists. It also prevents accidental reuse of an invalid or self-owned device pointer by skipping missing, error, or same-device cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a Hantro-specific helper to initialize the mem2mem device during probe instead of calling the generic initializer directly.
intent_record.what: In `hantro_probe()`, the initialization of `vpu->m2m_dev` was changed from a direct call to `v4l2_m2m_init(&vpu_m2m_ops)` to a call to `hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev(vpu)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, probe now obtains the mem2mem device through a helper that can incorporate device-specific setup or selection logic instead of always creating it with the same static ops table. This changes how the V4L2 mem2mem device is acquired and may allow the driver to use a preconfigured or shared m2m instance.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix probe error cleanup to use the correct v4l2 mem2mem device reference release API.
intent_record.what: In the error path of hantro_probe(), the cleanup call was changed from v4l2_m2m_release(vpu->m2m_dev) to v4l2_m2m_put(vpu->m2m_dev).
intent_record.how: This changes how the mem2mem device reference is released during probe failure cleanup, using the put-style API instead of the release-style API to match the expected ownership/refcounting semantics and avoid incorrect teardown behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the Hantro driver removal path to use the correct mem2mem device cleanup API.
intent_record.what: In hantro_remove(), the call to release the mem2mem device was changed from v4l2_m2m_release(vpu->m2m_dev) to v4l2_m2m_put(vpu->m2m_dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver now uses the reference-counted put operation for the mem2mem device during device removal, matching the expected lifetime management for that object and avoiding incorrect teardown semantics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an OF compatible table for IMX8MQ VPU G1/G2 shared resources.
intent_record.what: A new static constant device tree match table named `imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources` was added, marked `__initconst`, containing two compatible strings (`nxp,imx8mq-vpu-g1` and `nxp,imx8mq-vpu-g2`) plus the standard sentinel entry.
intent_record.how: This makes the two IMX8MQ VPU device variants explicitly identifiable as sharing resources through an OF match table, enabling later code to match these compatibles and apply shared-resource handling at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add shared VPU resource handling to the imx8mq G1 variant initialization.
intent_record.what: A new struct field assignment, `.shared_devices = imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources,`, was added to the `imx8mq_vpu_g1_variant` initializer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the G1 variant now explicitly references the shared VPU resource list, allowing the driver to account for shared devices when initializing or managing this variant.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add shared resource handling to the imx8mq G2 VPU variant so it uses the common shared device configuration.
intent_record.what: A new initializer field, `.shared_devices = imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources,`, was added to the `imx8mq_vpu_g2_variant` structure definition.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the IMX8MQ G2 Hantro variant will now reference the shared device/resource table, allowing the driver to account for resources that are shared with other VPU instances instead of treating this variant as standalone.

relevance_review.reason: The change documents that certain Hantro variant device IDs are shared and must not run concurrently, which directly matches the root cause that G1 and G2 on i.MX8MQ were incorrectly treated as independent and could decode at the same time.

The root cause is missing shared scheduling/coordination between i.MX8MQ Hantro G1 and G2 cores. This change adds shared resource handling and an OF compatible table for i.MX8MQ VPU G1/G2, which directly addresses that coordination issue.

The change only adds a missing OF platform header for device-tree platform support. It does not address the Hantro G1/G2 concurrency/scheduling issue or any shared coordination needed to prevent simultaneous decoding on i.MX8MQ.

The change introduces reuse of a shared V4L2 M2M device instead of treating instances independently, which directly relates to coordinating access and preventing concurrent operation of the Hantro G1/G2 cores.

The change only alters probe-time mem2mem initialization through a Hantro-specific helper. It does not add shared scheduling or coordination between the i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 cores, nor address the concurrent-decoding hardware limitation.

The changes only fix lifecycle cleanup/release API usage in probe/remove paths. They do not address the i.MX8MQ hardware limitation or add shared scheduling/coordination between Hantro G1 and G2 to prevent concurrent decoding.

The change adds shared VPU resource handling for the i.MX8MQ G1 variant, which directly matches the root cause: the driver previously lacked coordination for shared hardware resources between G1 and G2 cores, allowing invalid concurrent decoding.

The change adds shared resource handling for the i.MX8MQ G2 VPU variant and makes it use the common shared device configuration, which directly addresses the root cause of treating G1 and G2 as independent devices without coordination.

candidates.rationale: This variant definition is where the i.MX8MQ G1 core was configured as a standalone device. The root cause is that G1 and G2 actually share a hardware resource and must not run concurrently, so treating G1 as an independent variant contributes directly to the missing shared coordination.

This variant definition is the counterpart for the i.MX8MQ G2 core. It was also modeled as an independent device, which allowed concurrent scheduling with G1 despite the hardware limitation, directly embodying the vulnerability.

The probe path is where device instances are created and initialized independently. The root cause stems from missing shared-device handling in this lifecycle, so this function is the site where the lack of coordination is introduced.

vuln_statements.explanation: This probe function is where each VPU core was initialized as an independent device instance. Because i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 were not coordinated through a shared device/scheduler here, both could be brought up and used concurrently despite the hardware restriction.

This variant definition configured the i.MX8MQ G1 core as a standalone variant. That modeling contributed to the missing shared coordination between G1 and G2, allowing concurrent operation even though the hardware cannot support it.

This variant definition configured the i.MX8MQ G2 core as a standalone variant. Like the G1 variant, it treated the core as an independent device instead of a shared resource, which is the underlying cause of the unsafe concurrent decoding.
